name: Postpartum Support International (PSI)
summary: Support and resources for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders including postpartum depression.

sections.title: About Postpartum Support International
sections.text: Postpartum Support International (PSI) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to helping families suffering from perinatal mood and anxiety disorders, including postpartum depression. Founded in 1987, PSI provides direct peer support, educates healthcare professionals, and advocates for improved awareness and treatment. PSI's mission is to ensure that no family suffering from a perinatal mental health condition feels alone. The organization operates in all 50 states and over 40 countries.

sections.title: PSI Helpline
sections.text: PSI operates a confidential helpline at 1-800-944-4773 (English and Spanish) where you can leave a message and receive a return call within 24-48 hours from a trained volunteer who has personal experience with perinatal mental health conditions. For immediate crisis support, text HOME to 741741 to reach the Crisis Text Line. The PSI helpline is not a crisis line but provides warm, peer-based support and connections to local resources and providers who specialize in perinatal mental health.

sections.title: Perinatal Mental Health Conditions
sections.text: PSI provides resources for a range of perinatal mood and anxiety disorders including postpartum depression (PPD), postpartum anxiety, postpartum OCD, postpartum psychosis, postpartum PTSD, and pregnancy/prenatal depression and anxiety. These conditions can affect anyone during pregnancy or up to a year after birth—including fathers, partners, and adoptive parents. PSI emphasizes that perinatal mood disorders are common, temporary with proper treatment, and not the parent's fault.

sections.title: Support Groups and Coordinators
sections.text: PSI maintains a network of volunteer coordinators in every state and many countries who can connect you with local support groups, providers, and resources. Online support groups meet weekly via video conference, allowing parents to connect with others going through similar experiences regardless of location. Support groups are peer-led and provide a confidential space to share struggles, celebrate progress, and learn coping strategies. Groups are available in English and Spanish, with some groups specifically for fathers and partners.

sections.title: Finding Treatment Providers
sections.text: PSI's provider directory helps families find therapists, psychiatrists, and other mental health professionals who specialize in perinatal mental health. The organization also offers professional training certification for clinicians who want to specialize in treating perinatal mood disorders. PSI's website includes educational materials for healthcare providers on screening, diagnosis, and treatment of perinatal mental health conditions, helping ensure families receive appropriate evidence-based care.
